notes.about: Restack: Noahpinion, “Maybe the Rapture is already here”
notes.text: Noah Smith calls it “heavenbanned”: an AI that keeps you happy while nobody’s actually listening. Honestly, that’s half the relationships I’ve seen. AI just made it scalable.
"The plague" is trending, so here's my one rule: read the epidemiologist before the memes. @Katelyn Jetelina answers the top 8 questions. Panic is not a source.
"The exhaustion of being a good person" is everywhere this week (@ayushithakkar). Hot take: being the understanding one isn't a personality. It's unpaid labor. Who's your designated listener?
Couples who lasted answered each other's tiny "look at this" moments 86% of the time. Couples who split: 33%. Skip the rose petals. Look at the bird.

notes.about: Restack: The Wardrobe Edit, “A stylist told me what to buy for fall”
notes.text: Anna Newton's fall list is the rare shopping advice that actually saves you money. Read it before you buy another trend that's dead by November.

notes.about: Restack: The Humanity Archive, “You’ve Been Arguing With an Internet Bot”
notes.text: Jermaine Fowler says more than half of internet traffic is bots, which explains a lot about my comment section. Next time someone picks a fight with me online, I'm asking for a pulse first.
Over half of internet traffic is bots, per @thehumanityarchive. So that comment war you lost last week? Might have been a script. Honestly, a relief. Who's the most human-sounding bot you've fought?
Noah Smith says we're all "heavenbanned." So the AI utopia is just a group chat where everyone agrees with you and nobody's real? We already invented that. It's called LinkedIn. via @noahpinion
Being anti-AI is smarter than you think. The AI fight isn't about robots. It's about who gets paid when the machine does the work. The original Luddites knew that 200 years ago.
